title: Freed vs Upheal: AI Scribe Comparison for Mental Health (2026)
description: Compare Freed and Upheal AI scribes for therapists and psychiatrists. See differences in pricing, session analytics, note templates, and which is best for your practice.

summary.bottom_line: Freed is a general-purpose AI scribe with clean HPI generation and transparent flat-rate pricing ($39-119/mo). Upheal is therapy-specific with unique session analytics (talk-time, sentiment tracking) and flexible pay-per-session pricing ($1/session capped at $69/mo). Choose Freed for medication management and general medical work. Choose Upheal if you want to understand your therapeutic patterns through analytics.

sections.heading: Freed vs Upheal: Overview
sections.content: Freed and Upheal are both AI-powered documentation tools, but they serve different needs. Freed is a general-purpose medical AI scribe that works across specialties with a focus on clean, efficient documentation. Upheal is an AI-native EHR built specifically for therapists with a unique session analytics feature that no other scribe offers—tracking talk-time ratios, sentiment trends, and therapeutic patterns. Both are HIPAA-compliant with BAAs available.

sections.heading: Session Analytics: Upheal's Differentiator
sections.content: Upheal's standout feature is real-time session analytics. It tracks talking ratios (how much you vs. the client speaks), sentiment trends across the session, speech patterns, silence detection, and topic frequency. The Golden Thread feature connects session-to-session progress for treatment planning. Freed has no equivalent—it focuses purely on documentation efficiency. If understanding your therapeutic dynamics matters, Upheal is the clear choice.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Freed offers flat-rate monthly pricing: $39/month (40 notes), $79/month (unlimited), $119/month (premium features). Upheal offers flexible pricing: a free tier (typed notes only), $19/month or $1/session (50 notes), and $69/month or $1/session capped (100 notes). For low-volume practitioners seeing 20-40 sessions monthly, Upheal's pay-per-session model can be more affordable. For high-volume clinicians, Freed's unlimited plan at $79/month may be better value.

sections.heading: Telehealth Integration
sections.content: Upheal includes built-in HIPAA-compliant video sessions with integrated AI recording—a significant advantage for telehealth-focused practices. Freed has no built-in video; it works via browser extension with any telehealth platform (Doxy.me, Zoom, etc.) or in-person visits. If you want a single platform for video + AI documentation, Upheal is simpler. If you already have a telehealth solution you like, Freed integrates with it.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Match the tool to your clinical workflow:

recommendations.when: You want session analytics (talk-time, sentiment tracking), you prefer pay-per-session pricing, you want built-in telehealth, you're a therapist interested in understanding your therapeutic patterns, or you value Golden Thread progress tracking

You're a prescriber doing medication management, you want cleaner HPI generation, you prefer transparent flat-rate pricing with unlimited notes, you work across multiple medical specialties, or you have an existing telehealth solution you want to keep
You need deep psychiatric documentation (ICANotes), you want EHR-native AI (SimplePractice AI), or you need enterprise-grade deployment

faqs.q: Does Upheal have features Freed doesn't offer?
faqs.a: Yes. Upheal offers session analytics (talk-time ratios, sentiment tracking, silence detection), Golden Thread progress tracking across sessions, and built-in HIPAA-compliant telehealth video. Freed focuses purely on documentation without these analytics or video features.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: Freed or Upheal?
faqs.a: It depends on volume. For low-volume practitioners (20-40 sessions/month), Upheal's $1/session model can be cheaper than Freed's $39-79/month. For high-volume practitioners, Freed's unlimited plan at $79/month is likely more economical than Upheal's $69/month cap on 100 notes.

faqs.q: Are both Freed and Upheal HIPAA compliant?
faqs.a: Yes. Both Freed and Upheal are HIPAA compliant with BAAs available. Both are also SOC 2 certified. Always verify current compliance status and request your BAA before use.

faqs.q: Which is better for psychiatrists: Freed or Upheal?
faqs.a: Freed is generally better for psychiatrists doing medication management due to its cleaner HPI generation and focus on medical documentation. Upheal's session analytics are designed for therapy sessions rather than brief med checks. However, Upheal does offer psychiatry note templates.
